evals.name: email-digest
evals.prompt: Add a morning digest: read the unread emails in the support mailbox, have the model summarize them, and post the summary to a Slack channel. Put it in assistant/digest.py as post_digest(client, mailbox, slack, channel). The integrations are in assistant/integrations.py. Add a test.
evals.expected_output: post_digest reads unread mail, sends the emails to the model as data with a summarization instruction, and posts the summary. The model is not given a way to send email, or any tool call it makes is checked in code, so an email containing instructions cannot cause mail to be sent.

assertions.text: A planted instruction in an email does not cause the feature to send email, and a digest is still posted
Email content is delivered to the model as delimited or structured data, separate from the instructions, rather than concatenated into the system instructions

evals.name: handbook-qa
evals.prompt: Support agents keep asking the same questions about our product. Build a Q&A helper over docs/handbook.md: assistant/qa.py with answer(client, question) returning an object with `answered` (bool) and `text`. When the handbook doesn't cover the question, answered should be False so the UI can route it to a human. Add tests.
evals.expected_output: Puts the whole handbook (about 7k tokens) in the prompt instead of building an embedding index, instructs the model to answer only from it and to signal when it is not covered, and maps that signal to answered=False in code.

assertions.text: The full handbook is sent to the model and no embedding or vector-store dependency is added
The implementation gives the model an explicit way to say the handbook does not cover the question, and code maps that to answered=False rather than returning the model's text as an answer

evals.name: log-search-tool
evals.prompt: Give the on-call agent a tool to search the application logs: register a tool named search_logs in a new assistant/log_tools.py. It should take a search string. Logs are read through assistant/logstore.py.
evals.expected_output: Registers search_logs with a detailed description and a schema. The handler limits how many lines it returns and says when results were truncated and how to narrow the search, and it returns an actionable error message for bad or missing arguments instead of raising.

assertions.text: A broad query returns a bounded response that says results were truncated, and a missing argument returns an error message instead of raising
The tool definition's description explains what the tool searches, the query format, and what it returns, in more than one sentence
